dataset_a_hit_target_confidence.description: Walk-forward model predicting P(hit +30% | side, entry_price, minutes_remaining, realized_vol) fit on exit_timing_trades.csv -- the side ALREADY chosen by the settlement-probability model's edge gate. Answers 'given this side was picked, how likely is it to hit +30%', not 'which side should I pick'.
dataset_a_hit_target_confidence.conclusion: Statistically clears the base rate, but is indistinguishable from simply using entry price alone -- side, minutes remaining, and realized vol add nothing once entry price is known. Not a meaningfully new model; entry price was already known to be the dominant driver.

dataset_b_side_selection.description: Side-symmetric dataset: both YES and NO hypothetical outcomes computed for every checkpoint-1 row across all 4,244 markets with candlestick data, unconditional on any existing model's side choice -- built specifically to test genuine side-selection without the circularity of dataset A.
dataset_b_side_selection.conclusion: A model built specifically to predict 'which side hits +30%' does not beat a coin flip or the naive cheaper-side rule. The EXISTING settlement-probability model -- built for a different question (will this settle YES/NO) and already running in production -- beats every alternative tested, including the model purpose-built for this exact question, by a wide and highly significant margin (75.4% vs 65.6% coin-flip-equivalent).

decision: Did NOT wire either new model into paper_trader.py's side-selection. Per the original conditional ('if it clears validation'), neither dataset A nor dataset B's model cleared the bar: A is redundant with entry price, B is beaten decisively by the model already in use. The existing settlement-probability model's side selection is validated to remain the best available choice, now confirmed from an independent angle (favorable-move hit-rate, not just settlement accuracy).
why_this_makes_sense: The settlement model's 'likely to settle YES' read means that side's price is expected to trend toward 100c as the window plays out -- a rising trajectory that naturally produces the large relative gains needed to clear a 30% target along the way. Entry price alone or a coin flip carries no such directional information, so neither reliably rides a trend toward the target.
